answer: In an attestation graph, bounded-length random walks propagate trust while limiting unchecked influence across distance. A Sybil cluster joined to the honest graph by a narrow inlet has low conductance: few edges cross its boundary relative to its volume. Given fixed honest starting trust and degree-normalized transitions, spectral and min-cut bounds constrain how much voting weight can reach it; dense zephyr-like internal links cannot turn that river of attestations into disproportionate influence.
